lesson.title: Finance is cycles
lesson.html: Outputs in one process are inputs in another. Banks turn deposits into loans. Your spending is another person's income.

lesson.title: Check register
lesson.html: Order transactions by date. Deposits and + transfers add. Withdrawals and − transfers subtract. Keep a running balance.

lesson.title: Percent of a number
lesson.html: Convert the percent to a decimal and multiply: 50% of 10 = 0.5 · 10 = 5.

lesson.title: Comparing salaries
lesson.html: Subtract the salaries, multiply by the number of years, then subtract expenses like training or college.

pairs: Budget
An estimate of income and spending used to make financial choices; lists categories, $ and %
Check Register
A record of actual income and expenses used to verify budget tracking and account statements
Credit
The trust that lets people or banks provide goods, services or money with the assurance they'll be paid back later
Credit Card
A card used to borrow money to buy goods or services, to be paid back later
Credit History
A record of a borrower's responsible repayment of debts
Credit Report
A document describing a borrower's credit history, compiled by a private company
Debit Card
A card that is linked to a checking account
Deposit
Money placed into an account (+ on a check register)
Withdrawal
Money taken out of an account (− on a check register)
Transfer
Moving funds from one account to another; + or − on a check register
Fixed Expense
Costs that do not change from month to month
Variable Expense
Costs that change from month to month

list.q: Why is it important to know how budgets and check registers work?
list.a: Registers show how much money you have; budgets help you choose how to spend it
w: They are required by law for kids
list.why: Check registers ensure you know your balance; budgets let you make good choices.

list.q: A debit card is linked to…
list.why: A credit card borrows; a debit card spends your own money.

list.q: On a check register a deposit is…
list.why: Deposits and + transfers add; withdrawals and − transfers subtract.

list.q: How long do foreclosures and bankruptcies stay on your record?
list.why: They stay on your credit record for 7 years.

list.q: Which is NOT a primary way to pay for college?
list.a: A credit card with no limit
list.why: Primary ways: savings, scholarships, grants, student loans, work-study.

list.q: A document describing your credit history is a…
list.why: It is compiled by a private company but used by banks and others.

list.q: Good credit helps you get approved for…
list.a: Loans, a mortgage and credit cards
list.why: Credit history affects loans, mortgages, credit cards, leasing and hiring.
